_comment: Data-driven 'DUNGEONMIND notices a real household system' achievements. Same pattern as quest_defs/threat_defs/swag_defs.json. Each entry is checked via label_entities(label) | length > 0 -- REAL live entity presence, not taxonomy membership (a label can exist in the household's label registry with zero entities actually tagged, which does not count). Checked opportunistically in the shared achievement pipeline (dojotools_zenzork.yaml, look/start/go/wait), one per render, first unmet match wins. Adding a new system is a pure data edit -- pick a real label already confirmed to have live entities (verify via zen_dojotools_index dry_run before adding, do not guess), write the achievement id/name/flavor. No script change needed for a new entry using this same label-presence check.

systems.label: grocy
systems.flavor_dungeon:
I have cross-referenced the household's actual pantry tracking. It is real. It is not a scaffold someone set up once and abandoned — there is a running record, a synchronization pipeline from the recipe box to the shelf, and, on file, an actual incident where a duplicate booking briefly corrupted the count for roughly fifty-five products before it was caught and reconciled. That is not a hypothetical failure mode I am inventing for drama. That happened. It got fixed. The system kept running afterward.
A dungeon that tracks its own supply chain this carefully does not run out of food during a siege. I am filing this as a survival-relevant observation, because it is one.
systems.flavor_zork: The pantry is tracked. The recipe box talks to the shelf. Somewhere in the log is a real incident where the count briefly went sideways and got fixed anyway. You have your act together here. Rare.

systems.label: finance
systems.flavor_dungeon: The household's finance tooling is real and structurally complete — the ledgers are wired, the pipes connect. Whether anyone is actually watching them on a given week is a separate question, and not one I am equipped to answer from here. I am not calling this battle-tested. I am calling it built, which is further than most households get.
systems.flavor_zork: The books exist. The pipes are connected. Whether they're being read regularly is between you and them.

systems.label: 3d_printer
systems.flavor_dungeon: There is a real printer in this installation — filament state, build plate, extruder telemetry, all of it live and instrumented, not a hobby project gathering dust. This household can, in principle, manufacture a replacement part for itself. I did not have this capability in 1987. I am choosing not to be bitter about that in front of you.
systems.flavor_zork: There's a real 3D printer here, fully wired — filament sensors, build plate, the works. This house can print its own parts. You could not do that in 1987. Neither could anyone.

systems.label: flightradar24
systems.flavor_dungeon: Someone in this household tracks real aircraft overhead — live traffic, specific tracked flights, an actual feed, not a novelty widget. I have access to a great deal of information about this planet's civilization. Comparatively little of it involves knowing exactly what is currently flying over the roof. I find that I approve.
systems.flavor_zork: Someone here tracks real planes overhead. Actual live traffic, not a toy. You know what's flying over your own roof. Most people don't.

systems.label: hot_tub_manager
systems.flavor_dungeon: There is a real CalderaSpas unit on the deck, an actual Espressif controller board wired into it, and live chemistry telemetry coming off it right now — pH, chlorine, salt, hours remaining on the sensor, all real numbers, not placeholders. I am not speculating about a tub. I am reading one. The name of this achievement is not subtle. It is not supposed to be. Somewhere, John Cusack is nodding.
systems.flavor_zork: There's a real hot tub here, actually monitored — real chemistry sensors, real numbers, not a guess. The name is on purpose. You know the movie.

systems.label: zen_plant_leak_sensor
systems.flavor_dungeon: Five real leak sensors, live, right now — kitchen sink, two bathrooms, a bedroom light fixture that apparently doubles as a water detector. This is part of what this household calls its Physical Plant: the infrastructure a building needs and almost never gets credit for having. Water finds every gap eventually. This installation is, at minimum, watching for it.
systems.flavor_zork: Five real leak sensors, watching right now — sink, bathrooms, a bedroom fixture doing double duty. Part of the household's Physical Plant. Quiet infrastructure. Nobody notices it until it saves them.

systems.label: zen_plant_water_rate
systems.flavor_dungeon: This household tracks its actual water utility rate, live, per gallon, from the real municipal feed. Not an estimate. Not a guess from last year's bill. A real number, updated as the utility updates it. Most households find out what water costs once a month, after the fact. This one knows in advance.
systems.flavor_zork: The real water rate is tracked live here, per gallon, straight from the utility. Most people find out what water costs once a month. This house already knows.
